verdicts.reason: The source states Socket flagged the malicious release about 11 minutes after publication.
The source states the compromised release used a preinstall hook so payload could run during installation without importing the SDK.
The source states Socket flagged the malicious release about 11 hours after publication.
The source states Sonatype flagged the malicious release about 11 minutes after publication.
The source states Socket confirmed the worm stole credentials from thousands of CI environments.
The source states the attacker gained publish access through a phished maintainer password.
S1 asserts the Default suite runs 498 security queries covering 170 CWEs, as stated in doc:2509.
S2 asserts the Extended suite adds 131 queries covering 32 more CWEs, as stated in doc:2509.
S3 asserts Default + Extended cover 202 CWEs; equivalent to 170 + 32 if no overlap assumed, but the item does not specify overlap and the source does not confirm total 202.
S4 asserts Lambda now allows 30,000 durable operations per execution from 3,000, as stated in doc:4156.
S5 asserts the checkpoint payload limit raised from 256 KB to 1 MB, as stated in doc:4156.
S6 asserts Lambda functions can run for up to one year; this exact claim about duration is present in doc:4156.
S1 states a numeric total of 149,329 malicious open source packages in Q3 2026, which matches the document but the figure is from Sonatype; no conflicting data in cited source.
S2 cites 89.5% share for npm in Q3 2026, per the source; this matches the document.
S3 claims npm accounted for 96.6% of malicious packages with Q3 2026, which contradicts the source’s 89.5% for Q3; this is not supported by the cited document.
S4 asserts Sonatype attributes most Q3 malware to a single North Korean group; the provided document excerpt does not mention a specific threat group by name or attribution, so unsupported.
S5 claims since 2017 Sonatype logged more than 2 million malicious packages; the document states 1,960,846 total since tracking began, which is not ‘more than 2 million’ as an exact figure.
S6 repeats the total 1,960,846 malicious packages since 2017; this matches the document, so supported.
Item claims Mend.io moved 184 organizations and GitHub users onto Renovate Community OSS plan without request; source doc:4432 states 184 organizations and users were upgraded without request.
Item claims upgrade covers about 3,000 repositories with ~4 million stars; doc:4432 explicitly says 3,000 repositories and ~4 million stars.
Item claims 30,000 repositories; this contradicts the source which states 3,000; unsupported by cited source.
Item asserts Snyk upgraded 184 organizations to Renovate Community; doc:4432 mentions Mend.io, not Snyk, as upgrading; unsupported by cited source for Snyk.
Item claims Merge Confidence was made free for every Renovate user; doc:4432 states Merge Confidence is available (but not necessarily free) and may be Enterprise feature; unsupported as stated.

Item paraphrases that Community plan provides higher resource limits, more concurrency and Merge Confidence, which is Enterprise feature; doc:4432 describes these features for Community plan without asserting Enterprise exclusivity; interpretation ambiguous but supported by facts that Community plan provides these benefits; however stating ‘which is otherwise an Enterprise-plan feature’ adds a comparison not explicitly stated; uncertain but can be supported by source if it implies Enterprise-only previously.
S1 repeats Chainguard's claim of testing against 65 projects and validating 680 findings, which is stated in doc:88 and not contradicted by other sources in the item set.
S2 states a vulnerability behavior of vLLM before v0.31.0, which is a factual claim attributed to the Chainguard disclosure in doc:88.
S3 presents a numeric contradiction versus S1 (650 projects, 68 findings) not supported by doc:88; the document lists 65 projects and 680 findings.
S4 asserts Chainguard publishes exploit code; doc:88 explicitly states Chainguard does not publish exploit code.

S5 claims Chainguard has published advisories for all validated findings; doc:88 indicates advisories are published after fixes ship, not necessarily for all findings, and does not state all are published.
S6 aligns with doc:88: findings are reported to maintainers and advisories published after fixes ship; statement is supported by the source.
The source says Socket flagged the release approximately 11 minutes after publication.
The source identifies a preinstall hook that invokes the loader and says it can run during installation without importing the SDK.
The source says approximately 11 minutes, not 11 hours.
The source names Socket as the party that flagged the release, not Sonatype.
The source excerpt does not confirm credential theft from thousands of CI environments; that scale is missing.
The source excerpt does not state how the attacker gained publish access or mention a phished maintainer password.
The source reports Sonatype Research Labs logged 149,329 open source malware packages in Q3 2026.
The source states npm accounted for 89.5% in Q3, down from 96.6% in Q2.
The source states the opposite: npm's share declined from 96.6% in Q2 to 89.5% in Q3.
The cited source does not attribute most Q3 malware to a North Korean threat group.
The source says the total was nearly 2 million, specifically 1,960,846—not more than 2 million.
The source gives the total since tracking began in 2017 as 1,960,846 malicious packages.
The source states that the Default suite runs 498 security queries covering 170 CWEs.
The source states that the Extended suite adds 131 queries covering 32 more CWEs.
The total of 202 CWEs is computed from 170 and 32; the source does not state that combined figure.
The source states the limit increased from 3,000 to 30,000 durable operations per execution.
The checkpoint payload change appears in doc:4156, which this item does not cite; doc:2509 does not state it.
The source says durable functions help applications and AI workflows execute up to one year, not that AWS Lambda functions generally can.
The source says Mend.io upgraded 184 open source organizations and GitHub users without a request required.
The source gives about 3,000 repositories and roughly 4 million combined GitHub stars.
The source says about 3,000 repositories, not 30,000.
The source names Mend.io, not Snyk, as upgrading the organizations.
The source says the Community plan unlocks Merge Confidence for covered projects; it does not say it is free for every Renovate user.
The source says the Community plan provides higher resource limits, increased concurrency, and Merge Confidence, then available only on Enterprise.
The source states more than 65 projects and over 680 validated findings.
The source states that versions before v0.31.0 allowed one client to force other clients’ output on the same engine.
The source says more than 65 projects and over 680 findings, not more than 650 projects and over 68 findings.
The source explicitly says Chainguard does not publish exploit code.
The source says some findings are in coordinated disclosure and advisories follow fixes; it does not say advisories are published for all validated findings.
The source says Chainguard reports findings privately, waits for the fix to ship, then publishes an advisory with maintainers.
S1 repeats Chainguard’s claim from doc:88 that it has run its harness against more than 65 projects and validated over 680 findings, which is stated in the source.
S2 states a vulnerability detail about vLLM before v0.31.0, which is directly cited in doc:88.
S3 asserts Chainguard ran against 650 projects and 68 findings, which contradicts S1 (65 projects, 680 findings) and is not supported by doc:88.
S4 claims Chainguard publishes exploit code; doc:88 says Chainguard does not publish exploit code.
S5 claims Chainguard has published advisories for all validated findings; doc:88 describes publishing advisory after fixes but not for all prior findings, so not supported.
S6 aligns with doc:88: findings privately to maintainers and publish advisory after fix.
Document doc:4432 states Mend.io moved 184 open source organizations and GitHub users onto the Renovate Community (OSS) plan without them having to ask.
Document doc:4432 states the upgrade covers about 3,000 repositories with roughly 4 million combined GitHub stars.
Doc:4432 does not support a claim of 30,000 repositories; the source says about 3,000.
Doc:4432 mentions Mend.io, not Snyk, upgrading; the claim assigns the action to Snyk and is not supported by the cited source.
Doc:4432 states Mend.io made Merge Confidence free for every Renovate user.
Doc:4432 states the Community plan provides higher resource limits, more concurrency and Merge Confidence, an Enterprise-plan feature.
Doc:2509 states CodeQL Default suite runs 498 security queries covering 170 CWEs.
Doc:2509 states Extended suite adds 131 queries covering 32 more CWEs.
Doc:2509 implies Default (498) + Extended (131) cover 202 CWEs; while numbers are explicit for queries and CWEs, the total CWEs (202) is inferred from 170+32=202.
Doc:4156 states durable functions increases to 30,000 durable operations per execution from 3,000.

Doc:2509 does not state a checkpoint limit change; doc:4156 mentions checkpoint limits in its context; if doc:2509 does not mention, S5 would be unsupported. However the AWS new limit 1 MB is in doc:4156.
Doc:4156 states workflows can run up to one year.
S1 states Socket flagged the malicious release ~11 minutes after publication, which matches doc:2519 details.
S2 states a preinstall hook enabled payload during install per doc:2519.
S3 says ~11 hours after publication; doc:2519 indicates ~11 minutes, not 11 hours.
S4 says Sonatype flagged ~11 minutes after publication; doc:2519 mentions Socket flagged it; no mention of Sonatype in provided text, so this is unsupported.
S5 states the worm stole credentials from thousands of CI environments per doc:2519.
S6 states attacker gained publish access via a phished maintainer password per doc:2519.
S1 states a figure directly taken from doc:4: 149,329 malicious open source packages in Q3 2026.
S2 states a percentage (89.5%) attributed to npm in Q3 2026, cited in doc:4.
S3 asserts npm accounted for 96.6% in Q3 vs Q2; doc:4 provides 96.6% for Q2 and 89.5% for Q3, so S3 misstates the Q3 share.
S4 claims attribution to a single North Korean threat group; doc:4 does not mention such attribution.
S5 repeats a milestone figure: since 2017 Sonatype logged more than 2 million malicious packages, as per doc:4.
S6 repeats total since tracking began (1,960,846) as stated in doc:4.
